chunks: Ali, from his father, from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari who said:

We were with al-Ridha (peace be upon him) when we began discussing the intellect and moral virtue, so he said: O Abu Hashim, the intellect is a free gift from Allah while virtue is an effortful acquisition, whoever strives to acquire virtue is able to possess it but whoever strives to acquire intellect he achieves naught by that except further ignorance.

key_terms.حَبَاء: A free gift / A cloak of honor
key_terms.قَدِرَ: To be able / To have power over

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between intellect and moral virtue in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (peace be upon him) distinguishes between intellect (al-'aql), a divine gift, and moral virtue/education (al-adab), which is acquired through effort. He teaches that while one can master virtue through striving, striving for intellect itself may lead to increased ignorance, implying intellect is innate or divinely bestowed rather than merely learned. This hadith highlights the Shia epistemological view that true 'aql is a light from God, whereas 'adab is the disciplined cultivation of character.

en.ammaar-muslim: 5. [5/5] Usul al-Kafi: Ali from his father (Ibrahim b. Hashim) from Abi Hashim al-Ja’fari who said:

We were with al-Ridha عليه السلام when we began discussing about the intellect and moral virtue, so he said: O Abu Hashim, intellect is a free gift from Allāh while virtue is an effortful acquisition, whoever strives to acquire virtue is able to possess it but whoever strives to acquire intellect he achieves naught by that except further ignorance.
